jobs.description:
At ABB
, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

This position reports to:

Service Project Management Manager

__

In this role, you lead the end‑to‑end execution of Start‑up, Commissioning, and aftermarket service projects within the Data Center Services Center of Excellence. The portfolio includes Paralleling Switchgear and Protection & Control projects across the U.S. Electrification Service business. You set clear guidelines, define tasks and milestones, and drive performance through strong coordination, motivation, and feedback. You also safeguard and elevate customer satisfaction by ensuring all requirements, commitments, and project targets are consistently met, delivering high‑quality service at every stage of the engagement.

The work model for the role is: Remote in the US

This role is contributing to the Electrification Services Business Area
in the United States.

In this role your main accountabilities are:

Leads the project team by establishing execution approach and overseeing project hand-over, planning, monitoring and control activities for internal and external resources and accomplishing project goals
Managing the development of project planning documents
Monitoring projects to ensure best practices in cost control, resource efficiency and Health, Safety & Environment (HSE)
Analyzing and addressing project risks, and regularly disseminating lessons learned
Working with other functions to coordinate contract negotiations and claims with customers
Managing external suppliers to ensure availability of equipment, systems, material and services
Serve as an escalation point for project issues.
Achieving project deliverables and compliance with contract requirements
Building strong relationships with customers and stakeholders

Qualifications for the role:

A Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering highly preferred. Combination of education and relevant experience will be considered in lieu of.
3+ years of experience in the electrical industry working as a subject matter expert or project manager with paralleling switchgear, protection and control systems, electrical energy management systems, or electrical field services in the data center or power generation/distribution market
Demonstrated experience in management of project scope, cost, schedules and vendors/subcontractors
Knowledge of IEC61850, GE Zenith, ABB Protection and Control offerings (ZEE600, SSC600, PCM600 and associated relay hardware), Woodward Governor Controls, and/or Envisage energy management solutions are a plus
A collaborative, solution-focused approach, and strong written and spoken communication skills
Must have strong written and verbal communication skills in the English language
Ability to travel as necessary up to 20% of the time to support project kickoff and execution or as necessary to support successful execution of assigned projects
PMP Certification is a plus.
Candidates must already have work authorization that would permit them to work for ABB in the US

Why ABB?

What's In It For You

We want you to bring your full self to work—your ideas, your energy, your ambition. You’ll have the tools and freedom to grow your skills, shape your path, and take on challenges that matter. Here, your work creates impact you can see and feel, every day.

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
Lead complex projects. Align brilliant teams. Turn technical plans into measurable impact.

Technical Project Manager

Location: Fully Remote (USA)

About WhatConverts

WhatConverts is a B2B SaaS company specializing in marketing attribution and lead tracking solutions. We empower businesses to make data-driven decisions by providing deep insights into their marketing campaigns and helping them understand what drives conversions. As a remote-first company, we foster a mission-focused and performance-driven culture, valuing integrity, initiative, and innovation.

Position Overview

Great products don't ship on good ideas alone. They ship because someone turns big goals into a clear plan and keeps great teams moving. Here, that's you.

As our Technical Project Manager, you'll work where strategy meets engineering: weighing architectural tradeoffs, taming technical debt, and steering launches from first scope to production.

If you love asking sharp questions and spotting risk before anyone else does, you'll fit right in.

In This Role You’ll Get To

Turn business goals into clear technical requirements, milestones, and owners.
Run the delivery rhythm: work breakdowns, risk reviews, prioritization, and capacity planning that keep schedules predictable.
Own launches end to end, from production cutovers and deployments to rollback plans.
Connect product, sales, and leadership with developers, DevOps, QA, and architects, and de-risk dependencies across teams and vendors.
Catch bottlenecks and quality gaps early, and lead retrospectives that make every release better.
Give leaders a clear view through dashboards, OKRs, and crisp executive updates while keeping scope in check.

What We’re Looking For

3-6 years managing technical projects or programs in software or systems engineering.
Hands-on roots in software development, systems engineering, or DevOps, plus a solid grasp of APIs, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure.
Experience leading engineering teams through structured delivery cadences in Jira and Confluence.
A track record of shipping releases and production deployments across interdependent teams.
The ability to explain technical decisions to anyone, from engineers to executives.
Familiarity with security, compliance, and QA practices.
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. PMP, CSM, or similar certification is a plus.

﻿

Bonus points:
experience with martech, attribution, analytics, or integration-heavy products.

Company Benefits/Perks

Remote-First: Empowered to work agilely in a fully remote environment with no risk of office return.
Immediate Impact: From day one, take ownership of projects and make a direct impact.
Health & Wellness: 100% employer-paid premium medical, dental, vision, and life insurance.
401k with 5% Match: Secure your future with immediate vesting.
Employee Support: Access counseling, legal, and debt management services through our EAP.
Generous PTO & Flexible Time Off: Accrue PTO with additional days for tenure, plus up to 4 hours of flex time per week for personal matters.
Parental & Bereavement Leave: Paid leave for life’s important moments.
Volunteer Day: Give back with an annual volunteer day.
Diversity & Inclusion: Join a positive, supportive, and inclusive workplace.
Remote Work Perks: $100 monthly stipend to ensure your home office needs are met and company-provided devices.

Before You Apply You Should

Learn about our team
Read about what makes us different or watch a product overview
Read our reviews on G2

If you're passionate about working in a dynamic, fast growing company with smart colleagues and opportunities for development, come grow with WhatConverts.

Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is actively seeking a highly talented Senior Project Manager- Surface Transportation
for immediate employment in San Antonio, Texas or Austin, Texas.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:
Lead and manage programs that are medium to large in size and complexity or a defined part of a larger program, in support of the overall Program Manager.
Provide the organization with technical leadership and strategic direction for program delivery at a regional level.
Advocate for ethical and safe working practices.
Contributes to innovation in program management approaches and methodology to achieve marketplace differentiation.
Work with Regional leadership and Market Sector Leaders to identify new business opportunities and develop solutions to address them.
Identify areas of high risk and pro-actively takes actions to positively impact program outcomes.
Assess long-term and disruptive trends in their area of expertise. Proposes skill development approaches and workforce planning to deliver capabilities for the future.
Actively supports the attraction and retention of talent across area of expertise.
Accountable for overall financial success and delivery of AECOM Program Management agreement.

Qualifications

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

BA/BS + 10 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education, including 2 years of leadership.
Texas PE License.
US citizenship is a requirement for this posting.

Preferred Qualifications

15+ years of experience directly managing GEC/PMC project with TxDOT and other agencies including design-bid-build (DBB) and design-build (DB) projects.
The experience should demonstrate the ability to lead and administer GEC/PMC contracts effectively for agencies like TxDOT.
Experience serving as primary contact with TxDOT representatives and other clients, engaging in project scoping, addressing regulatory requirements, and fostering strong, long-term relationships.
Develop, monitor, and manage project scope, budget, and schedule from the proposal stage through final deliverables.
Coordination with local governments, contractors, sub-consultants, utilities, and other agencies to ensure seamless project execution and compliance.
Must have current TxDOT precertification in relevant work categories through the firm's administrative qualification with TxDOT's PEPS division.

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $140000 to $240000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. jobs.description:
Program Manager

Requisition ID req38214

Working Title Program Manager

Position Grade 13

Position Summary

The University of New Mexicos Project ECHO has a great opportunity for a Program Manager to join our New Mexico Community Peer Education Project (NMCPEP) Team!

The Program Manager will support the continued growth and expansion of NMCPEP and Behavioral Health Peer Initiatives (BHPI). This individual will oversee daily programmatic operations, supervise team members supporting both initiatives, and support the employment of several contractors and future staff as program growth continues.

As a successful Program Manager, you will play an active role in:

Overseeing the day-to-day operations of programs and activities related to CPEP and BHPI and statewide behavioral programming. Overseeing the coordination, preparation, and facilitation of the monthly teleECHO program for statewide partners and stakeholders.
Overseeing team travel to public health offices, probation and parole offices, and community-based organizations to accomplish CPEP and BHPI objectives and overseeing all follow-up actions for site visits to the states five Probation and Parole regional divisions.
Overseeing the management and coordination of referrals submitted by probation and parole staff for client services.
Ensuring BHPI programming aligns with evidence-based and peer-informed best practices, workforce development priorities, and program deliverables and implementing continuous quality improvement across both CPEP and BHPI programs.
Leading and supervising (2) Program Specialists, (1) Operations Specialist, contractors, and any additional FTEs as program growth necessitates. Designing positions, recruiting, hiring, training, supervising, and conducting annual evaluations. Reassigning staff duties as needed and supporting staff in new or evolving roles using a team-based leadership approach.
Providing regular one-on-one check-ins to address challenges, concerns, performance expectations, and professional development needs. Providing regular training and professional development opportunities for staff.
Serving as primary liaison to Behavioral Health providers, directors of probation and parole, re-entry divisions, peer organizations, state agencies, and other external constituencies on matters related to program activities and as primary liaison to internal teams supporting CPEP and BHPI, including Finance, Grants, Data, Replication, and IT.
Managing the creation, production, and delivery of promotional, educational, and informational materials related to program activities. Spearheading program replication efforts domestically and internationally, including oversight of curriculum and replication guide development.
Overseeing program promotion through media outlets and digital platforms in collaboration with Project ECHOs Communications Team.
Overseeing presentations at monthly partner launch trainings, Project ECHO events, and national or international conferences.
Working closely with the Executive Team Member and Senior Program Manager to plan, develop, and implement strategies for identifying and generating funding and resource opportunities.
Supporting the development of grant proposals and other funding efforts with agencies such as departments of behavioral health, corrections, probation and parole, and re-entry divisions.
Overseeing curriculum development and facilitation of virtual training for probation and parole staff, in-person training for new cadets at the corrections training academy, and 90-Day Onboarding Training for new community peer educators in accordance with the established peer certification requirements.
Overseeing the planning and implementation of the annual Peer Leadership Summit and other BHPI workforce development activities.
In collaboration with the Data Analyst and Operations Specialist, ensuring data, statistics, and narratives are accurately captured in iECHO, Smartsheet, Confluence, and other program systems. Supporting the development of monthly and quarterly reports demonstrating program functionality and best practices.

Project ECHO is unique and innovative center based within a vibrant academic community at the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center. Our mission is to democratize implementation of best practices with a goal of helping 1 billion people lead better lives by 2025. We are looking for mission-driven high performers who share similar values to join our team and help us achieve this goal.

Project ECHO is committed to democratizing implementation of best practices in healthcare, education and other areas where first mile professionals need support. We do this by training universities, nonprofits, and dedicated individuals on facilitation skills and how to set up robust virtual communities of practice to be able to scale their own expertise and missions to the benefit of their local communities. Over the past 20 years, Project ECHO and our partners have trained more than 1,000 partners who make up our global network of Universities, ministries of health, and NGOs around the world. Examples of programs we and others run include infectious disease control (Hepatitis C, HIV), mental health and addiction treatment, literacy, math, climate mitigation and many more.

Project ECHO is funded in part by philanthropic grants and gifts from organizations such as the GE Foundation, the Helmsley Charitable Trust, the Bristol Myers Squibb Foundation, the Merck Foundation, Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the US Government. Additionally, for programming benefitting New Mexico we receive support from the NM Legislature, the New Mexico Human Services Department and the New Mexico Department of Health.

Project ECHO prides itself on being a values-based organization and inclusive place to work. Our seven values include: Service to the Underserved, Democratization of Knowledge, Mutual Trust and Respect, Teamwork, Excellence and Accountability, Innovation and Learning and Joy of Work. We strive to find individuals who can embrace and exemplify these values. In addition, Project ECHO was named one of Albuquerques Top Three Best Places to Work in 2023. This award recognizes organizations of all sizes with exceptional climates, team atmospheres, benefits, and employee engagement. For more information and a brief overview of benefits available please visit Project ECHO Newsroom .

We work with partners all over the world and work hours outside of normal business hours may be required.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Science Strategy & Communications
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Accelerating scientific discovery is a core part of Anthropic's mission, and we believe the highest-leverage path to this is enabling researchers externally to use Claude effectively for their work. This involves communicating Claude’s rapidly improving scientific capabilities through outreach and editorial programs, as well as putting Claude in the hands of researchers through grants, ergonomic research tools, and access programs that help scientists do more with AI than was previously possible.

We’re hiring a Technical Program Manager to be the bridge between the researchers advancing Claude’s scientific capabilities and the outside scientific community. Embedded with the Discovery team, you’ll conceptualize and run the programs that get Claude into scientists’ hands and shape the Anthropic Science Blog, working with Communications, Editorial, Beneficial Deployments, and external partners such as universities, funders, and scientific societies.

This is a technical role, not a purely operational one. These programs already have strong operational and editorial owners. You bring research taste and a firsthand understanding of how academia works, so we’re looking for someone who has been a researcher themselves, ideally through a postdoc or beyond. You’ll have significant autonomy: once aligned with Discovery’s leads on strategy, you’ll drive decisions on what we fund, what we publish, and how we engage with academic communities

Key Responsibilities

Act as the interface between research and the outside world. Stay close to the researchers working on Claude's scientific capabilities and translate rapid capability gain into use by external researchers.
Help set Anthropic’s external science strategy. Recommend which scientific areas and communities we focus on, and how our programs, collaborations, and communications fit together
Guide the scientific direction of the Anthropic Science Blog. Work with researchers and the Editorial team to identify and source stories internal and external stories worth telling, draft and edit posts, and keep a steady cadence of high-quality science writing.
Drive forward external science programs. Design, launch, and run grants and access programs such as AI for Science grants and Team plan offerings for research groups, as well as partnerships with scientific foundations and grantmaking organizations. Work with Beneficial Deployments on programs aimed at the highest-impact scientific areas.
Gather feedback from scientific communities. Identify usage patterns and gather feedback on how researchers use Claude and what capability gaps exist, and turn it into concrete recommendations for research and product teams.

Minimum Qualifications

A PhD in a scientific or mathematical field, with a track record of original research
Demonstrated writing ability for both scientific domain and general-interest audiences, with enough understanding of how modern AI models are trained to write about them accurately.
Experience with the grants process, such as applying for and managing competitive funding, and ideally designing, reviewing, or administering funding programs
Deep engagement with frontier AI: you use these tools in your own work, understand where they're strong and where they fail, and take seriously the possibility that AI will transform every face of the scientific process within the next few years
Track record of driving multi-stakeholder projects to completion, and of coordinating people who are juggling other high-priority work. You’re resourceful, high-agency, and able to navigate ambiguity and shifting priorities.
Credibility with researchers: you can talk to scientists as a peer and understand how academic communities work, including their incentives, norms, and sensitivities
Fast learner who builds deep contextual understanding in unfamiliar scientific domains and can contribute meaningfully to discussions with researchers outside your own field.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience as a program officer, program director, or fellowship lead at a science funder, research agency, or philanthropy
Published science writing in outlets such as Quanta, Scientific American, or Physics Today, or a substantial public writing presence such as a blog or newsletter
Research experience that uses AI or ML methods, or that involves building scientific software, tools, or datasets
Experience building partnerships with scientific societies, journals, or research institutions
Familiarity with AI safety and responsible deployment, including dual-use considerations in fields like biology
Experience organizing conferences, workshops, or large coordinated launches

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$365,000—$435,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Location-based hybrid policy:

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. jobs.description:
Career Area

Job Description

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Cat Digital is the digital and technology arm of Caterpillar Inc., leveraging the latest technologies to build industry leading digital solutions for our customers and dealers. With over 1.5 million connected assets worldwide, our teams use data, technology, advanced analytics, telematics, and AI capabilities to help our customers build a better, more sustainable world.

Job Summary

The Senior Digital Project Manager leads the end-to-end delivery and global deployment of complex digital initiatives across the eCommerce and Owner’s Experience portfolio, with a primary focus on Cat Central. The role brings together cross-functional, regional, and dealer teams to manage risk, support readiness and adoption, and deliver strong business and customer outcomes.

Cat Central is Caterpillar’s flagship digital experience that connects customers with their equipment, data, services, and support tools, helping them manage and optimize operations throughout the equipment lifecycle.

What You Will Do

Lead the end-to-end planning, delivery, and global deployment of complex, high-visibility digital initiatives across multiple regions, markets, and dealer networks.
Develop and maintain integrated project and deployment plans, including scope, schedules, milestones, resources, dependencies, communications, and contingency plans.
Drive dealer-facing deployments for digital capabilities that require dealer integration or configuration, from readiness assessment through implementation and adoption.
Coordinate cross-functional teams across product, engineering, business, regional, and dealer organizations to align priorities, resolve issues, and deliver project outcomes.
Identify, assess, and mitigate risks, issues, and dependencies; monitor performance against plan and lead corrective action when needed.
Lead deployment readiness, release governance, go-live coordination, and post-deployment validation to ensure solutions meet quality, operational, and customer expectations.
Provide clear, timely updates to stakeholders and leadership on project status, decisions, risks, dependencies, and outcomes.
Ensure adherence to project management practices, quality standards, and governance requirements throughout the project and deployment lifecycle.

What You Will Have

Planning (Tactical and Strategic):
Experience translating business priorities into operational, tactical, and strategic plans. Develops integrated roadmaps that align scope, resources, milestones, dependencies, risks, and delivery commitments; monitors progress and adapts plans as priorities change.

Decision Making and Critical Thinking:
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex situations, organize relevant information, evaluate risks and alternatives, prioritize competing concerns, and make timely, informed decisions in ambiguous environments.

Data Gathering and Reporting:
Experience overseeing data collection and analysis, validating information for accuracy, evaluating options, and translating complex project data into clear reports, insights, and recommendations for stakeholders and leadership.

Implementation:
Demonstrated experience leading the implementation and adoption of digital capabilities, including technical and operational readiness, dealer or customer coordination, issue resolution, go-live support, user enablement, and post-deployment validation.

Digital Project Control and Reporting:
Extensive experience monitoring project performance, milestones, risks, issues, dependencies, and delivery schedules; adjusts plans, leads progress reviews, and communicates status, decisions, tradeoffs, and corrective actions.

Digital Project Management:
Extensive experience leading complex digital projects, aligning technical and business goals, managing quality and governance, and directing cross-functional teams. Applies project management practices and tools to manage schedules, resources, deliverables, reporting, and corrective actions.

Effective Communications:
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide concise status updates, communicate risks and decisions, and build trusted relationships with stakeholders and senior leaders.

Considerations for Top Candidates

Experience leading complex digital initiatives and global deployments across regions, markets, or dealer networks.
Ability to manage integrated plans covering scope, schedules, resources, dependencies, communications, risks, and contingencies.
Experience with dealer- or customer-facing deployments, including integration, readiness, implementation, adoption, go-live, and post-launch validation.
Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.
Strong judgment, problem-solving, and risk management skills in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
Knowledge of Agile, Waterfall and hybrid delivery methods, project governance, and quality standards.
Proactive, ownership-driven approach to anticipating needs and resolving issues early.
Customer-focused, continuous-improvement mindset.

What You Will Get

Working with a Fortune 100 leader, you can build your career on a global scale and take advantage of development opportunities with emerging technologies. We’ve created an inclusive environment for you to explore your passions, make an impact and do the work that really matters. Join Us.

About Caterpillar

Caterpillar Inc. is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives. For nearly 100 years, we’ve been helping customers build a better, more sustainable world and are committed to and contributing to a reduced-carbon future. Our innovative products and services, backed by our global dealer network, provide exceptional value that helps customers succeed.

jobs.title: Facilities CIP Program Manager (Water)
jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking a Facilities Design and Implementation Manager (Water)
who will manage the Program Management Office (PMO) Facilities Task Lane working for the Chicago Department of Water Management (DWM) to manage their $4+ billion Capital Improvement Plan (CIP). This leadership position is responsible for managing a team responsible for planning, managing, oversight, and execution of water infrastructure improvements necessary to effectively deliver nearly one billion gallons of drinking water per day to more than five million people in the City of Chicago and it suburban communities. The projects focus on twelve large water pumping stations; two of world’s largest water purification plants, intake structures, large conveyance tunnels, district facilities, and other critical hydraulic structures.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:
Serve as the Task Leader of the facilities team responsible for managing a team responsible for execution of DWM’s Capital Improvement Plan for both design and construction to include the following:
Preparation of scope of work and project deliverables
Development of project concept reports and cost estimates
Preparation of Request of Qualifications (RFQ) for procuring engineering and construction services
Consultant and Contractor qualifications assessment
Development of existing facility information and technical standards to the selected design consultant to assist in developing the required level of design effort necessary for the project
Review, evaluation, and negotiation of fee and schedule for performance of design.
Preparation of design and construction Notice to Proceed (NTP) letter to selected consultant and/or contractor.
Oversee and monitor work of the design consultant through submittals, design meetings, and document reviews.
Keep the Bureau of Engineering Services (BES) and other Bureaus as necessary apprised of project status and to include escalation of potential concerns or challenges as they arise.
Monitor design progress against project schedule and take corrective action as needed
Review interim cost estimates and monthly invoices by consultants and contractors. Take corrective action if consultant is over budget and/or behind schedule.
Arrange for distribution of interim submittals to reviewers and schedule meetings to discuss review comments.
Review construction estimates and prepares departmental requisitions for the procurement of construction services.
Coordinate project advertisement with the Department of Procurement Services (DPS).
Administer DWM’s responsibilities in the process of soliciting and reviewing competitive bids.
Conduct pre-bid conferences as required.
Provide written reports on the competitive bid process and recommendations of contract award as required by DPS.
Supervises technical professionals and other project managers including workload and staffing management.
Monitors and reports on financial and completion status of projects to client.
Serves as the primary source of communication between the PMO Facilities team and DWM Deputy Commissioners and the Chief Water Engineer from the Bureau of Engineering Services.
Performs all other duties as required by a supervisor such as recruitment, retention, performance evaluation, disciplinary action, and termination recommendations as deemed necessary.

At AECOM, our work in providing access to clean water enables communities to thrive and ecosystems to flourish, contributing to a resilient future. As a global leader in infrastructure consulting, we are at the forefront of significant water projects, with over 6,000 of the industry’s best minds driving innovation and technical excellence. Together, we develop solutions that are not only best in the world, but best for the world.

With an acceleration in infrastructure investment, your bold ideas and global expertise have never been more crucial. Join our dynamic team, where innovation, career growth, and collaboration are celebrated. Enjoy the freedom to grow with customizable career paths, water-specific technical and professional development and the potential to contribute to transformational projects worldwide. Discover your #H2Opportunity

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

BA/BS + 8 YORE or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Professional Engineering (PE) license in Illinois or the ability to obtain by reciprocity within first 6 months of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil or environmental engineering or a related discipline and 15+ years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
15+ years of experience in Water/Wastewater as an engineer and/or project manager.
Strong interpersonal, people management, and communication skills.
Experience managing large ($500M+) Capital Improvement Plans for municipal water and wastewater entities.
Candidates must have proven interpersonal skills, including client interaction, public speaking, and persuasive ability; strong project financial management along with ability to lead diverse, multi-disciplined teams.

Additional Information

Sponsorship is not offered for this position now or in the future.
Relocation not available.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $175000 to $225000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Position Description

Senior Project Manager Security

Position Description

Note: This job posting is only open to native level or near-native level Dutch speakers.
If you are not proficient in Dutch, please have a look at our other job postings instead!

Lead what matters when it matters most.

We’re looking for a Senior Project Manager who thrives in complex, high-stakes environments and knows how to turn security strategy into real-world impact. In this role, you won’t just manage timelines and budgets—you’ll drive critical security initiatives that protect organizations, data, and people.

You’ll work at the intersection of cybersecurity, risk, and business transformation, guiding multidisciplinary teams and engaging senior stakeholders. From implementing security frameworks to overseeing large-scale transformation programs, you bring clarity, structure, and momentum where it counts.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Your role in our team

As a Senior Project Manager, you will:

Act as the central point of coordination between security experts, IT teams, and business stakeholders
Lead or interact with multidisciplinary teams (e.g. cybersecurity specialists, architects, engineers, risk/compliance officers) toward shared project goals
Translate security strategy and requirements into actionable plans for the team
Ensure alignment between technical delivery and business objectives
Facilitate communication across teams, removing silos and resolving dependencies
Drive planning, prioritization, and execution of security initiatives
Identify risks and bottlenecks early, enabling everybody involved to respond proactively
Report progress, challenges, and outcomes to senior stakeholders
Promote a security-first mindset within the broader project and organization.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

How you strengthen our team

What sets you apart:

5+ years of experience delivering IT cloud infrastructure and/or cybersecurity projects
Strong track record in international project environments, ideally within global enterprises
Excellent stakeholder management skills, able to influence and align business, IT, and external partners (including C-level)
Proven ability to work independently, drive initiatives, and deliver with a pragmatic, hands-on mindset
Experience managing third-party vendors and overseeing project/service contracts
Clear and effective communication skills in English and Dutch (written and verbal), even in complex or high-pressure situations

Your working environment

As a Senior Project Manager – Security, you will join the Banking business unit within our Financial Services sector.

The banking landscape is evolving rapidly—becoming more open, competitive, and heavily regulated. At the same time, banks face increasing pressure to reduce costs, meet rising customer expectations, and comply with strict privacy and cybersecurity requirements.

In this environment, security is no longer optional—it’s a core business priority. Banks depend on secure, resilient, and future-proof IT systems to protect their reputation, maintain customer trust, and stay competitive.

At CGI, you will lead impactful security initiatives for leading Dutch banks, driving the development of secure digital ecosystems. You’ll work with modern technologies and ways of working—such as Agile, DevOps, Cloud, and AI—where security by design is central.

Working at CGI means shaping the digital future of banking, where innovation and security go hand in hand.

Why CGI?

CGI is one of the world's largest IT consultancy firms. Our people keep the Netherlands running. Government agencies, banks, (aero-) space, infrastructure organizations and energy and manufacturing companies are clients of CGI. We work on interesting projects that touch the daily lives of millions of people. We are present regionally, augmented with global domain knowledge, our ecosystem, and colleagues spread all over the world. We are proud of the impactful projects that we, together with our colleagues, make a success.

At CGI, we continuously examine the impact of new technologies on our service delivery and the solutions we develop for our clients. Developments in the fields of AI and automation also play an increasingly important role in this regard.

At CGI, we place great value on diversity and inclusion, as this not only promotes collaboration but often leads to better results. We look forward to your contribution to our team!

Work in small self-managing teams consisting of experts in your field
Take control of your own career with the space to continue developing yourself
You work with the latest technologies
An excellent salary and attractive secondary employment conditions
Immediate permanent contract
Part-time possibilities
And the opportunity to become a CGI shareholder

Join our team of experts and apply now!

We will contact you as soon as possible. Questions about the position? Ask them to Arend-Jan Buzepol, Director Consulting Services via arend-jan.buzepol@cgi.com

For more information about the application procedure, please contact recruiter Jana Kreckova via jana.kreckova@cgi.com

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Come join our team—one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world.

Contribute to the continuous improvement of delivery methodologies, project templates, tools, and best practices.

What We’re Looking For

Excellent project planning, execution, stakeholder management, and communication skills.

Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify and mitigate risks early.

Role overview

We are seeking a highly analytical, commercially minded and results-driven Software Licence Compliance Intelligence Manager
to join our Global Licence Compliance team.
This role is suited to a data analyst with a strong understanding of software licence compliance and the ability to turn intelligence into well-founded investigative and commercial decisions. The successful candidate will analyse data gathered through software intelligence and monitoring tools—including platforms such as Revenera and Cylynt—to identify, assess and prioritise potential non-compliance and infringement opportunities.
The role requires more than producing analysis or reports. The analyst will assess the reliability and significance of available information, use sound judgement to determine appropriate next steps, and identify opportunities that can support business development and market expansion. This includes working with relevant stakeholders to decide which leads warrant further investigation, escalation or commercial follow-up.
The successful candidate will play a central role in managing and interpreting software piracy data collected through our monitoring technologies, identifying potential copyright infringements and transforming technical information into actionable Licence Compliance opportunities.
Our mission is to reduce non-compliant software use by proactively addressing infringements while fostering constructive engagement with businesses to create opportunities for the future.

Key responsibilities

Data Analysis & Intelligence

Manage, process, analyse and interpret large volumes of software usage and piracy-related data collected through different monitoring technologies.
Perform data cleaning, processing, and validation to improve investigation accuracy
Use and interpret intelligence gathered through software monitoring and compliance tools, including Revenera and Cylynt, or comparable platforms.
Conduct OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence) research to gather evidence on infringement cases.
Maintain accurate records of investigations and compliance cases.
Use data visualisation and business intelligence tools to identify trends, monitor performance and communicate findings.
Identify patterns, anomalies, leads and market signals that may indicate potential non-compliance or reveal opportunities for further investigation and business development.

Opportunity Validation & Commercial Assessment

Investigate and validate potential software piracy cases by assessing the quality, reliability and relevance of technical and other available evidence.
Evaluate & validate opportunities based on commercial potential, market conditions, enforcement feasibility and relevant compliance or reputational considerations.
Use sound judgement to prioritise leads and recommend whether they should be pursued, investigated further, referred for legal or compliance review, or closed.
Identify evidence gaps and specify what additional information or validation is required; communicate recommendations and potential business value to business-development, sales and other relevant stakeholders.

Project Management & Operational Improvement

Manage relationships with technology providers and other external partners involved in data collection and investigation.
Support the development and implementation of new technologies and automated workflows to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the Licence Compliance Program.
Monitor operational performance, identify bottlenecks and recommend improvements.
Help assess the usefulness, accuracy and operational value of intelligence tools and data sources and recommend improvements where appropriate.

Collaboration & Reporting

Skills & Requirements

Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in data analysis, business intelligence, software licence compliance, software piracy investigations, anti-piracy intelligence or a related field, with a demonstrated understanding of how compliance intelligence supports case assessment and follow-up.
Working knowledge of software intelligence or monitoring platforms such as Revenera, Cylynt or comparable tools, with the ability to interpret and assess the intelligence they generate.

**Location:** UAE — Remote
**Employment Type:** Full-Time
**Experience Level:** Junior / Entry-Level
**Department:** Cybersecurity / Security Operations
**Salary Range:** AED 12,000–16,000 per month *(proposed; subject to experience and employer budget)*

## About the Role

We are seeking a motivated and analytical **Junior Security Operations & Threat Intelligence Analyst** to support our cybersecurity team in identifying emerging threats, reviewing security alerts, and helping protect business systems and digital assets.

This role is suitable for an early-career IT or cybersecurity professional who wants to develop practical skills in threat intelligence, security monitoring, and threat analysis. The successful candidate will work with experienced security professionals and receive guidance on established tools, processes, and industry practices.

## Key Responsibilities

* Monitor cybersecurity news, threat advisories, and emerging attack techniques.
* Assist with collecting and analyzing threat intelligence from trusted sources.
* Review security alerts and identify potentially suspicious activities.
* Support the investigation and documentation of indicators of compromise (IOCs).
* Help correlate threat intelligence with security logs and monitoring data.
* Research malware campaigns, phishing threats, and common attack methods.
* Assist with preparing threat reports and security briefings for internal teams.
* Maintain records of threat indicators, vulnerabilities, and relevant security incidents.
* Collaborate with security operations, IT, and incident response teams.
* Follow established procedures for handling sensitive information and escalating potential threats.

## Requirements

* Diploma or bachelor's degree in IT, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related discipline; equivalent practical knowledge may be considered.
* Basic understanding of cybersecurity principles, networking, and common cyber threats.
* Familiarity with phishing, malware, suspicious domains, and social engineering techniques.
* Basic knowledge of security logs, incident reporting, or SIEM concepts.
* Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Good written communication and report-writing abilities.
* Willingness to learn new security tools and threat analysis techniques.
* Ability to work independently and collaborate with a remote team.

**Entry-level candidates are encouraged to apply.** Relevant coursework, internships, personal cybersecurity labs, and beginner certifications are beneficial but not mandatory.

## Preferred Skills

* Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK and common attacker techniques.
* Introductory knowledge of SIEM platforms such as Microsoft Sentinel or Splunk.
* Awareness of threat intelligence platforms and IOC analysis.
* Basic understanding of Python, PowerShell, or other scripting tools.
* Familiarity with cybersecurity resources such as CISA advisories and reputable threat research publications.
* Relevant introductory certifications or training in cybersecurity.

## What We Offer

* Proposed salary of AED 12,000–16,000 per month, depending on qualifications and experience.
* Remote working opportunities, subject to the employer's location and employment policies.
* Structured onboarding and professional development.
* Mentorship from experienced cybersecurity professionals.
* Exposure to threat intelligence research and security operations workflows.
* Opportunities to develop practical threat analysis and incident response skills.
* A collaborative environment that encourages continuous learning.

## How to Apply

Submit your CV with details of your IT background, cybersecurity training, relevant projects, internships, or practical lab experience.

Use **“Junior Security Operations & Threat Intelligence Analyst – Remote”** as the application subject line.

Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

About WhatConverts

WhatConverts is a B2B SaaS company specializing in marketing attribution and lead tracking solutions. Position Overview

Great products don't ship on good ideas alone. They ship because someone turns big goals into a clear plan and keeps great teams moving. Here, that's you.

As our Technical Project Manager, you'll work where strategy meets engineering: weighing architectural tradeoffs, taming technical debt, and steering launches from first scope to production.

If you love asking sharp questions and spotting risk before anyone else does, you'll fit right in.

In This Role You’ll Get To

Turn business goals into clear technical requirements, milestones, and owners.
Run the delivery rhythm: work breakdowns, risk reviews, prioritization, and capacity planning that keep schedules predictable.
Own launches end to end, from production cutovers and deployments to rollback plans.
Connect product, sales, and leadership with developers, DevOps, QA, and architects, and de-risk dependencies across teams and vendors.
Catch bottlenecks and quality gaps early, and lead retrospectives that make every release better.
Give leaders a clear view through dashboards, OKRs, and crisp executive updates while keeping scope in check.

What We’re Looking For

3-6 years managing technical projects or programs in software or systems engineering.
Hands-on roots in software development, systems engineering, or DevOps, plus a solid grasp of APIs, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure.
Experience leading engineering teams through structured delivery cadences in Jira and Confluence.
A track record of shipping releases and production deployments across interdependent teams.
The ability to explain technical decisions to anyone, from engineers to executives.
Familiarity with security, compliance, and QA practices.
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. PMP, CSM, or similar certification is a plus.

﻿

Bonus points:
experience with martech, attribution, analytics, or integration-heavy products.

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is actively seeking a highly talented Senior Project Manager- Surface Transportation
for immediate employment in San Antonio, Texas or Austin, Texas.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:
Lead and manage programs that are medium to large in size and complexity or a defined part of a larger program, in support of the overall Program Manager.
Provide the organization with technical leadership and strategic direction for program delivery at a regional level.
Advocate for ethical and safe working practices.
Contributes to innovation in program management approaches and methodology to achieve marketplace differentiation.
Work with Regional leadership and Market Sector Leaders to identify new business opportunities and develop solutions to address them.
Identify areas of high risk and pro-actively takes actions to positively impact program outcomes.
Assess long-term and disruptive trends in their area of expertise. Proposes skill development approaches and workforce planning to deliver capabilities for the future.
Actively supports the attraction and retention of talent across area of expertise.
Accountable for overall financial success and delivery of AECOM Program Management agreement.

Qualifications

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

BA/BS + 10 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education, including 2 years of leadership.
Texas PE License.
US citizenship is a requirement for this posting.

Preferred Qualifications

15+ years of experience directly managing GEC/PMC project with TxDOT and other agencies including design-bid-build (DBB) and design-build (DB) projects.
The experience should demonstrate the ability to lead and administer GEC/PMC contracts effectively for agencies like TxDOT.
Experience serving as primary contact with TxDOT representatives and other clients, engaging in project scoping, addressing regulatory requirements, and fostering strong, long-term relationships.
Develop, monitor, and manage project scope, budget, and schedule from the proposal stage through final deliverables.
Coordination with local governments, contractors, sub-consultants, utilities, and other agencies to ensure seamless project execution and compliance.
Must have current TxDOT precertification in relevant work categories through the firm's administrative qualification with TxDOT's PEPS division.

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $140000 to $240000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Program Manager

Requisition ID req38214

Working Title Program Manager

Position Grade 13

Position Summary

The University of New Mexicos Project ECHO has a great opportunity for a Program Manager to join our New Mexico Community Peer Education Project (NMCPEP) Team!

The Program Manager will support the continued growth and expansion of NMCPEP and Behavioral Health Peer Initiatives (BHPI). This individual will oversee daily programmatic operations, supervise team members supporting both initiatives, and support the employment of several contractors and future staff as program growth continues.

As a successful Program Manager, you will play an active role in:

Overseeing the day-to-day operations of programs and activities related to CPEP and BHPI and statewide behavioral programming. Overseeing the coordination, preparation, and facilitation of the monthly teleECHO program for statewide partners and stakeholders.
Overseeing team travel to public health offices, probation and parole offices, and community-based organizations to accomplish CPEP and BHPI objectives and overseeing all follow-up actions for site visits to the states five Probation and Parole regional divisions.
Overseeing the management and coordination of referrals submitted by probation and parole staff for client services.
Ensuring BHPI programming aligns with evidence-based and peer-informed best practices, workforce development priorities, and program deliverables and implementing continuous quality improvement across both CPEP and BHPI programs.
Leading and supervising (2) Program Specialists, (1) Operations Specialist, contractors, and any additional FTEs as program growth necessitates. Designing positions, recruiting, hiring, training, supervising, and conducting annual evaluations. Reassigning staff duties as needed and supporting staff in new or evolving roles using a team-based leadership approach.
Providing regular one-on-one check-ins to address challenges, concerns, performance expectations, and professional development needs. Providing regular training and professional development opportunities for staff.
Serving as primary liaison to Behavioral Health providers, directors of probation and parole, re-entry divisions, peer organizations, state agencies, and other external constituencies on matters related to program activities and as primary liaison to internal teams supporting CPEP and BHPI, including Finance, Grants, Data, Replication, and IT.
Managing the creation, production, and delivery of promotional, educational, and informational materials related to program activities. Spearheading program replication efforts domestically and internationally, including oversight of curriculum and replication guide development.
Overseeing program promotion through media outlets and digital platforms in collaboration with Project ECHOs Communications Team.
Overseeing presentations at monthly partner launch trainings, Project ECHO events, and national or international conferences.
Working closely with the Executive Team Member and Senior Program Manager to plan, develop, and implement strategies for identifying and generating funding and resource opportunities.
Supporting the development of grant proposals and other funding efforts with agencies such as departments of behavioral health, corrections, probation and parole, and re-entry divisions.
Overseeing curriculum development and facilitation of virtual training for probation and parole staff, in-person training for new cadets at the corrections training academy, and 90-Day Onboarding Training for new community peer educators in accordance with the established peer certification requirements.
Overseeing the planning and implementation of the annual Peer Leadership Summit and other BHPI workforce development activities.
In collaboration with the Data Analyst and Operations Specialist, ensuring data, statistics, and narratives are accurately captured in iECHO, Smartsheet, Confluence, and other program systems. Supporting the development of monthly and quarterly reports demonstrating program functionality and best practices.

Project ECHO is unique and innovative center based within a vibrant academic community at the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center. Our mission is to democratize implementation of best practices with a goal of helping 1 billion people lead better lives by 2025. We are looking for mission-driven high performers who share similar values to join our team and help us achieve this goal.

Project ECHO is committed to democratizing implementation of best practices in healthcare, education and other areas where first mile professionals need support. We do this by training universities, nonprofits, and dedicated individuals on facilitation skills and how to set up robust virtual communities of practice to be able to scale their own expertise and missions to the benefit of their local communities. Over the past 20 years, Project ECHO and our partners have trained more than 1,000 partners who make up our global network of Universities, ministries of health, and NGOs around the world. Examples of programs we and others run include infectious disease control (Hepatitis C, HIV), mental health and addiction treatment, literacy, math, climate mitigation and many more.

Project ECHO is funded in part by philanthropic grants and gifts from organizations such as the GE Foundation, the Helmsley Charitable Trust, the Bristol Myers Squibb Foundation, the Merck Foundation, Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the US Government. Additionally, for programming benefitting New Mexico we receive support from the NM Legislature, the New Mexico Human Services Department and the New Mexico Department of Health.

Project ECHO prides itself on being a values-based organization and inclusive place to work. Our seven values include: Service to the Underserved, Democratization of Knowledge, Mutual Trust and Respect, Teamwork, Excellence and Accountability, Innovation and Learning and Joy of Work. We strive to find individuals who can embrace and exemplify these values. In addition, Project ECHO was named one of Albuquerques Top Three Best Places to Work in 2023. This award recognizes organizations of all sizes with exceptional climates, team atmospheres, benefits, and employee engagement. For more information and a brief overview of benefits available please visit Project ECHO Newsroom .

We work with partners all over the world and work hours outside of normal business hours may be required.

See The Position Description For Additional Information.
