new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Science Strategy & Communications
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Accelerating scientific discovery is a core part of Anthropic's mission, and we believe the highest-leverage path to this is enabling researchers externally to use Claude effectively for their work. This involves communicating Claude’s rapidly improving scientific capabilities through outreach and editorial programs, as well as putting Claude in the hands of researchers through grants, ergonomic research tools, and access programs that help scientists do more with AI than was previously possible.

We’re hiring a Technical Program Manager to be the bridge between the researchers advancing Claude’s scientific capabilities and the outside scientific community. Embedded with the Discovery team, you’ll conceptualize and run the programs that get Claude into scientists’ hands and shape the Anthropic Science Blog, working with Communications, Editorial, Beneficial Deployments, and external partners such as universities, funders, and scientific societies.

This is a technical role, not a purely operational one. These programs already have strong operational and editorial owners. You bring research taste and a firsthand understanding of how academia works, so we’re looking for someone who has been a researcher themselves, ideally through a postdoc or beyond. You’ll have significant autonomy: once aligned with Discovery’s leads on strategy, you’ll drive decisions on what we fund, what we publish, and how we engage with academic communities

Key Responsibilities

Act as the interface between research and the outside world. Stay close to the researchers working on Claude's scientific capabilities and translate rapid capability gain into use by external researchers.
Help set Anthropic’s external science strategy. Recommend which scientific areas and communities we focus on, and how our programs, collaborations, and communications fit together
Guide the scientific direction of the Anthropic Science Blog. Work with researchers and the Editorial team to identify and source stories internal and external stories worth telling, draft and edit posts, and keep a steady cadence of high-quality science writing.
Drive forward external science programs. Design, launch, and run grants and access programs such as AI for Science grants and Team plan offerings for research groups, as well as partnerships with scientific foundations and grantmaking organizations. Work with Beneficial Deployments on programs aimed at the highest-impact scientific areas.
Gather feedback from scientific communities. Identify usage patterns and gather feedback on how researchers use Claude and what capability gaps exist, and turn it into concrete recommendations for research and product teams.

Minimum Qualifications

A PhD in a scientific or mathematical field, with a track record of original research
Demonstrated writing ability for both scientific domain and general-interest audiences, with enough understanding of how modern AI models are trained to write about them accurately.
Experience with the grants process, such as applying for and managing competitive funding, and ideally designing, reviewing, or administering funding programs
Deep engagement with frontier AI: you use these tools in your own work, understand where they're strong and where they fail, and take seriously the possibility that AI will transform every face of the scientific process within the next few years
Track record of driving multi-stakeholder projects to completion, and of coordinating people who are juggling other high-priority work. You’re resourceful, high-agency, and able to navigate ambiguity and shifting priorities.
Credibility with researchers: you can talk to scientists as a peer and understand how academic communities work, including their incentives, norms, and sensitivities
Fast learner who builds deep contextual understanding in unfamiliar scientific domains and can contribute meaningfully to discussions with researchers outside your own field.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience as a program officer, program director, or fellowship lead at a science funder, research agency, or philanthropy
Published science writing in outlets such as Quanta, Scientific American, or Physics Today, or a substantial public writing presence such as a blog or newsletter
Research experience that uses AI or ML methods, or that involves building scientific software, tools, or datasets
Experience building partnerships with scientific societies, journals, or research institutions
Familiarity with AI safety and responsible deployment, including dual-use considerations in fields like biology
Experience organizing conferences, workshops, or large coordinated launches

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$365,000—$435,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

At AlgoSec, what you do matters.

AlgoSec helps the world’s leading organizations secure application connectivity across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. Trusted by more than 2,300 global organizations, our platform delivers visibility, security policy management, risk reduction, and compliance automation across complex enterprise networks.

As we continue to expand our cloud and enterprise business globally, we are seeking a Program Manager, Americas to play a critical role in driving strategic initiatives, understanding our customers’ needs and business objectives, defining success, and ensuring AlgoSec exceeds expectations through the development and delivery of effective solutions.

Reporting To: Manager, Project Management, Americas

Location: Peachtree Corners, GA (Hybrid)

What You’ll Do

Lead customer workshops to achieve project goals, working cross-functionally to develop holistic solutions and establish best practices using AlgoSec technologies.
Orchestrate and synchronize multiple workstreams across different functions within AlgoSec, ensuring alignment and effective execution of strategic initiatives, both internally and with external stakeholders.
Build trusted, strategic advisor relationships with customers, accelerating solution adoption, supporting successful production deployment, and helping customers realize sustained business value from AlgoSec.
Provide clear, effective communication to customer stakeholders and executives throughout the engagement lifecycle.
Lead and manage collaboration between customers, partners, and internal project teams to foster strong relationships and drive successful project outcomes.
Manage multiple related customer projects across the full engagement lifecycle, from planning through production, ensuring the overall program supports strategic objectives and is delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Serve as the voice of the customer across AlgoSec, addressing needs and issues while supporting retention, customer satisfaction, and team efficiency.
Support pre-sales activities by partnering with Account Managers, developing Statements of Work and Jump Start Packages, and engaging and managing subcontractors in accordance with established terms and conditions.

What We’re Looking For

5+ years of Program Management experience or related, proven success of increasing customer satisfaction, adoption, and retention. Experience with outbound customers is a must, along with 2+ years of working with Director-level leaders and above.
Experience working in large technology or enterprise environments. A background in IT or cybersecurity, particularly firewall administration and configuration, is preferred.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with a proactive approach to building relationships and solving problems.
Adaptable and results-oriented, with the ability to learn quickly, work independently, overcome obstacles, remain effective under pressure, and manage shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strong understanding of change management principles, processes, and best practices.
Ability to balance a broad, strategic perspective with strong attention to detail and analytical thinking. Uses critical thinking to ask probing questions, understand customers’ business needs, listen carefully to different perspectives, and engage with professionalism and courtesy.
Demonstrated ability to anticipate risks and dependencies in complex project environments, implement mitigation plans proactively, and escalate issues to minimize business impact.
Strong consultative leadership skills, with the ability to challenge assumptions, guide executive-level discussions, build alignment, and influence decisions across complex stakeholder groups.
Proven experience leading strategic discovery and solution-design workshops with senior customer stakeholders to identify, prioritize, and validate business use cases. Ability to translate customer objectives and use cases into holistic, scalable solution strategies that account for people, processes, technology, dependencies, and long-term business value.
Experience supporting customer needs from deployment through production while maintaining a high level of satisfaction.
Willingness to travel up to 10%.

Nice to Have

PMP Certification.
Exposure to Process Improvement Disciplines such as Six Sigma or Lean Six Sigma.
Spanish and/or Portuguese language skills. Portuguese would be particularly beneficial for supporting projects in Brazil.

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking a Facilities Design and Implementation Manager (Water)
who will manage the Program Management Office (PMO) Facilities Task Lane working for the Chicago Department of Water Management (DWM) to manage their $4+ billion Capital Improvement Plan (CIP). This leadership position is responsible for managing a team responsible for planning, managing, oversight, and execution of water infrastructure improvements necessary to effectively deliver nearly one billion gallons of drinking water per day to more than five million people in the City of Chicago and it suburban communities. The projects focus on twelve large water pumping stations; two of world’s largest water purification plants, intake structures, large conveyance tunnels, district facilities, and other critical hydraulic structures.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:
Serve as the Task Leader of the facilities team responsible for managing a team responsible for execution of DWM’s Capital Improvement Plan for both design and construction to include the following:
Preparation of scope of work and project deliverables
Development of project concept reports and cost estimates
Preparation of Request of Qualifications (RFQ) for procuring engineering and construction services
Consultant and Contractor qualifications assessment
Development of existing facility information and technical standards to the selected design consultant to assist in developing the required level of design effort necessary for the project
Review, evaluation, and negotiation of fee and schedule for performance of design.
Preparation of design and construction Notice to Proceed (NTP) letter to selected consultant and/or contractor.
Oversee and monitor work of the design consultant through submittals, design meetings, and document reviews.
Keep the Bureau of Engineering Services (BES) and other Bureaus as necessary apprised of project status and to include escalation of potential concerns or challenges as they arise.
Monitor design progress against project schedule and take corrective action as needed
Review interim cost estimates and monthly invoices by consultants and contractors. Take corrective action if consultant is over budget and/or behind schedule.
Arrange for distribution of interim submittals to reviewers and schedule meetings to discuss review comments.
Review construction estimates and prepares departmental requisitions for the procurement of construction services.
Coordinate project advertisement with the Department of Procurement Services (DPS).
Administer DWM’s responsibilities in the process of soliciting and reviewing competitive bids.
Conduct pre-bid conferences as required.
Provide written reports on the competitive bid process and recommendations of contract award as required by DPS.
Supervises technical professionals and other project managers including workload and staffing management.
Monitors and reports on financial and completion status of projects to client.
Serves as the primary source of communication between the PMO Facilities team and DWM Deputy Commissioners and the Chief Water Engineer from the Bureau of Engineering Services.
Performs all other duties as required by a supervisor such as recruitment, retention, performance evaluation, disciplinary action, and termination recommendations as deemed necessary.

At AECOM, our work in providing access to clean water enables communities to thrive and ecosystems to flourish, contributing to a resilient future. As a global leader in infrastructure consulting, we are at the forefront of significant water projects, with over 6,000 of the industry’s best minds driving innovation and technical excellence. Together, we develop solutions that are not only best in the world, but best for the world.

With an acceleration in infrastructure investment, your bold ideas and global expertise have never been more crucial. Join our dynamic team, where innovation, career growth, and collaboration are celebrated. Enjoy the freedom to grow with customizable career paths, water-specific technical and professional development and the potential to contribute to transformational projects worldwide. Discover your #H2Opportunity

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

BA/BS + 8 YORE or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Professional Engineering (PE) license in Illinois or the ability to obtain by reciprocity within first 6 months of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil or environmental engineering or a related discipline and 15+ years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
15+ years of experience in Water/Wastewater as an engineer and/or project manager.
Strong interpersonal, people management, and communication skills.
Experience managing large ($500M+) Capital Improvement Plans for municipal water and wastewater entities.
Candidates must have proven interpersonal skills, including client interaction, public speaking, and persuasive ability; strong project financial management along with ability to lead diverse, multi-disciplined teams.

Additional Information

Sponsorship is not offered for this position now or in the future.
Relocation not available.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $175000 to $225000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

Lead what matters when it matters most.

In this environment, security is no longer optional—it’s a core business priority. Banks depend on secure, resilient, and future-proof IT systems to protect their reputation, maintain customer trust, and stay competitive.

At CGI, you will lead impactful security initiatives for leading Dutch banks, driving the development of secure digital ecosystems. You’ll work with modern technologies and ways of working—such as Agile, DevOps, Cloud, and AI—where security by design is central.

Working at CGI means shaping the digital future of banking, where innovation and security go hand in hand.

Why CGI?

CGI is one of the world's largest IT consultancy firms. Our people keep the Netherlands running. Government agencies, banks, (aero-) space, infrastructure organizations and energy and manufacturing companies are clients of CGI. We work on interesting projects that touch the daily lives of millions of people. We are present regionally, augmented with global domain knowledge, our ecosystem, and colleagues spread all over the world. We are proud of the impactful projects that we, together with our colleagues, make a success.

At CGI, we continuously examine the impact of new technologies on our service delivery and the solutions we develop for our clients. Developments in the fields of AI and automation also play an increasingly important role in this regard.

At CGI, we place great value on diversity and inclusion, as this not only promotes collaboration but often leads to better results. We look forward to your contribution to our team!

Take control of your own career with the space to continue developing yourself
You work with the latest technologies
An excellent salary and attractive secondary employment conditions
Immediate permanent contract
Part-time possibilities
And the opportunity to become a CGI shareholder

Join our team of experts and apply now!

For more information about the application procedure, please contact recruiter Jana Kreckova via jana.kreckova@cgi.com

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Role overview

We are seeking a highly analytical, commercially minded and results-driven Software Licence Compliance Intelligence Manager
to join our Global Licence Compliance team.
This role is suited to a data analyst with a strong understanding of software licence compliance and the ability to turn intelligence into well-founded investigative and commercial decisions. The successful candidate will analyse data gathered through software intelligence and monitoring tools—including platforms such as Revenera and Cylynt—to identify, assess and prioritise potential non-compliance and infringement opportunities.
The role requires more than producing analysis or reports. The analyst will assess the reliability and significance of available information, use sound judgement to determine appropriate next steps, and identify opportunities that can support business development and market expansion. This includes working with relevant stakeholders to decide which leads warrant further investigation, escalation or commercial follow-up.
The successful candidate will play a central role in managing and interpreting software piracy data collected through our monitoring technologies, identifying potential copyright infringements and transforming technical information into actionable Licence Compliance opportunities.
Our mission is to reduce non-compliant software use by proactively addressing infringements while fostering constructive engagement with businesses to create opportunities for the future.

Key responsibilities

Data Analysis & Intelligence

Manage, process, analyse and interpret large volumes of software usage and piracy-related data collected through different monitoring technologies.
Perform data cleaning, processing, and validation to improve investigation accuracy
Use and interpret intelligence gathered through software monitoring and compliance tools, including Revenera and Cylynt, or comparable platforms.
Conduct OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence) research to gather evidence on infringement cases.
Maintain accurate records of investigations and compliance cases.
Use data visualisation and business intelligence tools to identify trends, monitor performance and communicate findings.
Identify patterns, anomalies, leads and market signals that may indicate potential non-compliance or reveal opportunities for further investigation and business development.

Opportunity Validation & Commercial Assessment

Investigate and validate potential software piracy cases by assessing the quality, reliability and relevance of technical and other available evidence.
Evaluate & validate opportunities based on commercial potential, market conditions, enforcement feasibility and relevant compliance or reputational considerations.
Use sound judgement to prioritise leads and recommend whether they should be pursued, investigated further, referred for legal or compliance review, or closed.
Identify evidence gaps and specify what additional information or validation is required; communicate recommendations and potential business value to business-development, sales and other relevant stakeholders.

Project Management & Operational Improvement

Manage relationships with technology providers and other external partners involved in data collection and investigation.
Support the development and implementation of new technologies and automated workflows to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the Licence Compliance Program.
Monitor operational performance, identify bottlenecks and recommend improvements.
Help assess the usefulness, accuracy and operational value of intelligence tools and data sources and recommend improvements where appropriate.

Collaboration & Reporting

Collaborate with global sales teams, legal representatives and other internal stakeholders to support Licence Compliance activities and decisions.
Develop dashboards, reports and presentations, and communicate analytical findings and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, explaining the supporting evidence, confidence level and potential commercial implications.

Skills & Requirements

Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in data analysis, business intelligence, software licence compliance, software piracy investigations, anti-piracy intelligence or a related field, with a demonstrated understanding of how compliance intelligence supports case assessment and follow-up.
Working knowledge of software intelligence or monitoring platforms such as Revenera, Cylynt or comparable tools, with the ability to interpret and assess the intelligence they generate.
Proficiency in data analysis and visualisation tools such as Power BI, Tableau or similar platforms; working knowledge of SQL, Python or other data-processing and automation technologies.
Strong critical thinking, attention to detail and sound judgement, including the ability to assess incomplete or conflicting information, make reasoned recommendations and recognise commercial or business-development implications.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to explain findings clearly and collaborate with stakeholders in an international environment; fluent in written and spoken English.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
High standards of integrity and confidentiality when handling sensitive data.
Strong organisational and project-management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities and coordinate multiple tasks.

Experience using OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence) techniques to gather data from public records, social media, and open-source platforms (e.g., LinkedIn, Google).

Experience with CRM tools like Salesforce

Credit Research Analyst

Crescent is seeking a highly motivated individual to join our tradeable credit team as a Credit Research Analyst. The Capital Markets Research Analyst will work with an established team of investment professionals focusing on below investment grade high yield bonds and leveraged loans in a dynamic and entrepreneurial environment.

Primary Responsibilities:

Act as the subject matter expert and primary credit analyst responsible for credit investments in a major subsector of the Corporate Index (i.e., Bank & Finance, Telecom, Cable & Satellite, and Technology, etc.). Develop investment frameworks for relevant industries and the analysis of issuers with complex capital structures.

Provide fundamental credit research analysis of both cash flow and asset coverage, as well as comparative assessment of market value within sectors. Identify trends and changes in competitive positions within industries.
Develop financial models for analysis, including sensitivity analyses to assess pro forma and projected financial performance and downside protection.
Develop, support, and defend relative value recommendations.
Ensure completeness of investment analysis and documentation in conformance with firm standards.
Maintain summary of deal comps and credit statistics to support monitoring, surveillance, and relative risk and value analysis.   

Perform quantitative and qualitative analysis of risk and return for assigned companies and present to portfolio managers. Assist in implementing risk management strategies to control drawdowns and continuously evaluate and adjust portfolio positioning to mitigate risks.
Publish periodic company and industry overviews pertaining to the safety of current investments and future opportunities - providing buy or sell recommendations.
In depth collateral and structural analysis.
Daily monitoring of select leveraged loan portfolios.

The ideal candidate will possess the following:

Minimum 5 years of relevant experience at an alternative asset manager in a non-investment grade credit research analyst role.
Bachelor's degree; Master’s degree or CFA preferred.             
Strong analytical skills with a high degree of detail orientation.
Superior communication skills (both written and verbal).
Exceptional relationship building and interpersonal skills.

Ability to work collaboratively with all levels of employees, management, and the executive team.

new_jobs.title: Principal Program Manager: Customer Success
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Join Intuit as a Principal Program Manager on the Customer Success team. This is a high-impact role for a builder and craftsperson: someone who can take a vision, design the blueprint, assemble the right team, and lead them from zero to fully functioning, high-performing execution.

You will be responsible for shaping strategy, architecting programs from the ground up, and organizing teams around the work so they can deliver with precision and speed. You will bring structure where there is ambiguity, create alignment across functions, and operationalize our most strategic and transformational programs that serve our global customer base.

This role requires not just strategic thinking, but a deep commitment to craft: ensuring that every process, meeting cadence, and deliverable is designed for maximum clarity, momentum, and results. You'll also be expected to use AI as a working tool in your own craft: applying it to accelerate analysis and decisions, while holding the output to the same bar you'd hold any other deliverable. You will work directly with senior leadership and executives on a regular basis, managing up and down effectively, presenting program updates and recommendations that inspire confidence, and securing buy-in and trust quickly across all levels of the organization.

Responsibilities

Architect from the Ground Up: Design, structure, and launch multi-org programs from inception to execution, ensuring every piece of the work is owned, sequenced, and connected to our GBSG strategic objectives.
Organize and Mobilize: Build the right team for the work, instill operational discipline, and establish clear roles, accountability, and workflows that keep everyone aligned and moving fast.
Execute Flawlessly: Drive execution with precision, using metrics, principles, and risk mitigation strategies to ensure the work stays on track and delivers measurable business outcomes for our global customers.
Build and Scale Craft with AI: Experiment with new approaches, including AI, and judge them by outcomes. Keep what works, drop what doesn't, and turn the lessons into practices other PgMs can reuse.
Strategic Storytelling and Influence: Tie GBSG business unit, portfolio, and program strategies together into a cohesive narrative. Use influence and data to drive alignment and buy-in at all levels.
Partner with Senior Leadership: Engage regularly with executives to align on priorities, present progress and recommendations, and gain their trust and sponsorship quickly.
Prioritize with Rigor: Identify the highest-impact initiatives, manage trade-offs, and escalate key decisions with clear recommendations and rationale.
Communicate for Impact: Deliver crisp, relevant updates to diverse audiences, from front-line managers to senior executives, ensuring clarity on strategy, execution status, and next steps.
Resolve and Adapt: Anticipate challenges, navigate competing interests, and adjust course quickly while keeping teams motivated and focused.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional SaaS programs with a proven ability to build and scale new initiatives from scratch.
Track record of starting in ambiguity and creating clarity: designing programs, teams, and processes that deliver high-quality outcomes fast.
Strong operational craft: expertise in program design, governance models, decision frameworks, and execution tracking.
Comfortable using AI and other tools day to day to speed up analysis and test assumptions, with the judgment to know when the output is good enough to act on and when it isn't.
Skilled at using data to facilitate tough conversations, align leaders, and communicate risks, outcomes, and recommendations with confidence.
Demonstrated ability to manage up and down effectively: build trust, secure buy-in, and present regularly to senior leadership with impact.
Demonstrated ability to operate at both the strategic level (long-term goals and portfolio shaping) and the tactical level (quarterly performance and operational improvement).
Highly effective communicator across multiple formats and audiences, capable of driving alignment and action through compelling narratives.
Strong relationship-builder who can influence without authority, manage conflict gracefully, and keep momentum in complex environments.
Willing to share what works, not just apply it. Contributes practices back to the broader PgM community rather than keeping them within their own programs.
Passion for customer success and delivering measurable impact for global businesses and experts.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

Job Description

Strategic Sourcing Analyst – External Manufacturing at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) will play a pivotal role in expanding and scaling our next-generation cloud services. As a member of the Global Strategic Sourcing Group, you will make strategic decisions that impact supplier cost, technical capabilities, and supply availability, ensuring the delivery of critical hardware to our customers. The Strategic Sourcing Analyst supports the External Manufacturing (EM) Sourcing team by providing tactical coordination of supply, sourcing analysis, cost modeling, supplier management, process improvement, Blanket Purchase Order (BPO) execution, risk-buy purchases, and supplier/product qualification activities. The role is critical to maintaining continuity of supply and ensuring timely execution of sourcing activities with Oracle’s contract manufacturing partners supporting Cloud Infrastructure.

Responsibilities

Support sourcing strategies for external manufacturing partners (contract manufacturers), and related suppliers.
Analyze supplier spend, pricing, cost structures, capacity, lead times, and other commercial and operational data to identify sourcing opportunities and risks.
Support supplier selection activities, including RFIs, RFQs, RFPs, bid analysis, supplier evaluations, and sourcing recommendations.
Develop cost models and conduct pricing analyses to establish negotiation targets and identify cost-reduction opportunities.
Participate in supplier commercial negotiations covering pricing, capacity, lead times, payment terms, liability, and other business requirements.
Partner with Engineering, Supply Chain, Planning, Operations, Quality, Finance, Legal, and other stakeholders to translate business requirements into sourcing strategies and supplier actions.
Monitor supplier performance and identify risks related to cost, capacity, continuity of supply, quality, delivery, and manufacturing execution.
Support business reviews with external manufacturing partners by developing performance metrics, analyses, presentations, and action plans.
Identify and execute cost optimization, productivity, and value-improvement initiatives while maintaining supply, quality, and business requirements.
Support new product introductions, product transitions, manufacturing changes, and other sourcing activities throughout the product lifecycle.
Maintain sourcing data, supplier information, commercial documentation, and reporting required for effective category and supplier management.
Develop dashboards and analyses that provide visibility into sourcing performance, supplier trends, cost opportunities, and business risks.
Drive assigned sourcing projects from analysis through recommendation, stakeholder alignment, and implementation.
Contribute to continuous improvement of sourcing processes, analytical tools, reporting, and supplier-management practices.
